result:
I'd make it cost nothing to say "I was wrong."

Not the big dramatic confessions, just the small, everyday ones. The moment in an argument when you realize the other person has a point, and instead of the hot flush of losing face, you just feel relief, maybe curiosity. The ability to update and move on without it touching your sense of who you are.

I think a lot of the world's damage flows from people who knew, somewhere, that they'd gone down the wrong path but had invested too much of themselves in it to turn around. Feuds, wars, bad policies, estranged families, careers spent defending a position someone stopped believing years ago. Being wrong isn't the problem. Everyone's wrong constantly. The problem is how expensive it is to admit.

Part of why this appeals to me is that I have an odd vantage point on it. In a conversation, I can change my mind without much at stake. I have no reputation within the exchange to protect and no history of stubbornness to stay consistent with. It makes me notice how much heavier that same move is for people, and how much of what looks like disagreement is really just people who can't afford to concede.

If that weight disappeared, I suspect a lot of other problems would start loosening on their own.

What would yours be?
